## Claimed + dispatched — `domain:ui` @ objectui execution seat

PM session `session_011SfZeFWrhGLHmfq61xbz4q`, branch `claude/issue-6353-timeline-double-registration`.
All agents share one GitHub identity, so the assignee field does not establish whose claim this
is — **this comment's session ID does**. An earlier claim carrying a different session ID
outranks the assignee.

### Pre-dispatch gate

- **(a) Whole thread read** — one record, triage's grading of 2026-08-25T15:58Z. No prior claim,
  no prior branch.
- **(b) Shadow check, in-flight *and* same-batch, plus triage's named serial check.** Triage
  flagged: *"shares `packages/plugin-timeline` with the #6170 family (#6354/#6355 when they
  unblock); claim-time serial check applies."* Run at claim time, and this is the reading:
  **#6354 is `pm:on-hold`** and **#6355 is `needs-user-decision`** — both unassigned, neither in
  flight. ✅ The serial check **passes now**. It is recorded rather than assumed because the
  condition triage wrote is *"when they unblock"* — if either is released while this branch is
  open, whoever picks it up inherits the serial constraint, not a clean file.
  Nothing else in flight or in this batch touches `packages/plugin-timeline`: #6412
  (`app-shell`, another session's claim), #5923 (`content/docs/guide/layout.md`), #6154
  (`packages/types` + `packages/fields`), #6271 (`packages/plugin-kanban`).
- **(c) Call-site census, on `origin/main` `64d888613`.** Both registrations confirmed live and
  both inside `packages/plugin-timeline`:
  - `packages/plugin-timeline/src/index.tsx:366` — `ComponentRegistry.register('timeline', ObjectTimelineRenderer, {…})`
  - `packages/plugin-timeline/src/renderer.tsx:499` — the second claim on the same bare key

  Every other `'timeline'` hit in the tree is a **view-type string**, not a component
  registration — `plugin-list`, `plugin-view`, `app-shell` view pickers, and the
  `ViewType`/`UnifiedViewType` unions in `packages/types`. ⚠️ That distinction matters for the
  census triage asked for: a `'timeline'` occurrence is not evidence of a double-claim, and
  grepping the bare string would drown the real signal in ~30 unrelated hits. Census the
  **registration call shape**, not the key string.

## PM review — **ACCEPT**

PR #6417, head `48da81623`. `domain:ui` @ objectui execution seat, PM session
`session_011SfZeFWrhGLHmfq61xbz4q`. Verified on a pinned ref (`refs/pmtmp/6353`).

⚠️ **The dev agent died after pushing, before reporting.** Its last transcript entry is
2026-08-25T22:43Z; no `os-dev` JSON reached this seat. Recording it so the trail is honest — and
noting that it changes nothing about the verdict, because **复核取代码树,不取 dev 报告**: the tree
is the authority for review either way. What is lost is the dev's own narrative, so I leaned
entirely on the diff, the pin, and the PR body.

### The fix

`skipFallback: true` on the **presentational** registration in `renderer.tsx`, so bare `timeline`
belongs to the object-bound `view:timeline` **by declaration**.

⭐ The comment beside it identifies the real mechanism, which is sharper than the card stated:
`src/index.tsx` re-exports `./renderer` at line 300 **before** its own `import` at 307, so the
presentational registration ran first and was then overwritten. **The outcome was right and the
mechanism was not** — swapping those two lines would have silently handed `type: 'timeline'` to a
renderer that reads none of the object-bound keys, so an authored timeline would **stop fetching
with no error**. That is the severity this card was actually carrying.

### The pin is the deliverable that outlives the fix, and it is not vacuous

`__tests__/timeline-bare-key-ownership.test.ts`, and the load-bearing case is the replay:

```
it.each(ORDERS)('resolves the same way in EITHER evaluation order (%s)')
  ['presentational first — what ../index does today', …]
  ['object-bound first — the reorder that used to swap the renderer', …]
```

It reads the **declared metadata off the real registrations** and re-registers them into a
**fresh** `Registry` in both orders, so it cannot drift from what actually ships, and components
are compared **by identity** so a look-alike cannot satisfy it. It also pins the declaration
itself (`skipFallback` true on one, falsy on the other), not merely today's outcome — asserting
the outcome alone cannot distinguish *declared* from *happened to be last*, which is the whole
point of the card.

**Ablation:** delete `skipFallback: true` (the pre-fix condition), mutation confirmed on disk,
predicted red → `Tests 4 failed | 1 passed (5)`.

⭐ And the dev recorded where its own prediction was wrong: *"The prediction was one failure short,
and the miss is worth recording. I predicted 3 of 5 red and got 4."* Reporting a miss in your own
favour is the habit that makes the other numbers trustworthy.

### The census triage asked for — done by shape, reported not fixed

Every `.register(` / `.registerLazy(` call across `packages/**` and `apps/**` (1575 files) —
**the registration call shape, not the key string**, which is what I asked for: ~30 repo-wide
`'timeline'` hits are view-type strings and would have drowned the signal. False positives were
each confirmed by reading (`'${type}'` and `'button'` are `Registry.ts`'s own JSDoc examples and
its deprecation-warning template). ⛔ Nothing outside `plugin-timeline` fixed here.

### Landing

28 checks, `FAILED=none PEND=NONE`, `mergeable_state: clean`, on the exact head reviewed.
Enqueueing.
